FantasyPros has Ka'imi Fairbairn first among all kickers this week, so the position is fine from here; the ranking is a record of games already played. Spend your claims on tight end instead. Your worst position is run by the best kicker in football.

proj:under:4258173:4695883.title: The projections have been a touch generous
proj:under:4258173:4695883.text: Your starters have come in slightly under forecast on the season, and it is mostly two names pulling opposite ways. Nico Collins has been beating his number all year while Jalen Coker has been well short of his, and Coker has started more often than that gap deserves. One of them is overperforming quietly and the other is underperforming out loud.

lineup:C:4360761:w8.title: The bench has been the better half
lineup:C:4360761:w8.text: This is the thing to fix: a lot of points have spent this season on your bench. Week 8 is the one, when Tre Tucker took a receiver slot and scored nothing while Michael Wilson put up a big number behind him. The weeks since have been kinder. A zero and a big number, filed in the wrong order.

pos:TE3:QB7.title: Tight end is the strength, quarterback the gap
pos:TE3:QB7.text: George Kittle has the tight end slot comfortably handled, and quarterback ranks seventh, so that is where a claim helps most. FantasyPros does still have Jared Goff inside their top ten quarterbacks this week, so the position is serviceable rather than broken, and he is the only one you roster. A one-man quarterback room is fine right up until it is not.

proj:under:-16016:4360761.title: The projections have been overrating your starters
proj:under:-16016:4360761.text: Your lineup has fallen well short of its forecasts on the season, and the split is instructive: the Vikings defense keeps beating its number while Michael Wilson keeps missing his by a wide margin. Start the defense with confidence and treat the Wilson projections as a suggestion. A defense outscoring a receiver is a model asking for help.

lineup:B:4696981:w10.title: Good calls, one recent exception
lineup:B:4696981:w10.text: Your lineup decisions rank among the best in this league, so there is little to change. Week 10 is the fresh one: Kenneth Walker started at running back and did not score, while Cam Skattebo put up a big afternoon on your bench. Walker has been ruled out twice since, which is its own kind of answer.

pos:WR1:TE8.title: Best receivers in the league, worst tight ends
pos:WR1:TE8.text: Your receivers rank first and your tight ends rank last, so every claim should go to tight end until that changes. Chig Okonkwo is unowned and FantasyPros has him inside their top ten this week, which is the cheapest fix on the board. CeeDee Lamb has been carrying a position that should not need carrying.

proj:over:4430878:4360248.title: Your starters are beating the forecasts
proj:over:4430878:4360248.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has been outrunning his projection all season while Kyle Pitts has been well short of his. Keep riding Smith-Njigba. The roster figured this out before the model did.

lineup:C:4036378:w9.title: Two quarterbacks, one slot
lineup:C:4036378:w9.text: Start here. The best available lineup has outscored the one you started by a wide margin this season. Week 9 is the case in point, when Josh Allen started at quarterback and Jordan Love outscored him from your bench. Two good quarterbacks is a nice problem and an expensive one.

pos:DST1:FLEX8.title: Best defense in the league, worst flex
pos:DST1:FLEX8.text: Your defense ranks first and your flex, the wild-card slot that takes a runner or a receiver, ranks last, so that slot is where attention pays. Emmett Johnson and a returning Jonathon Brooks are the two names most likely to fix it from inside the roster. A first-place defense cannot cover for a last-place flex, though it has been trying.

proj:under:-16034:4429160.title: The forecasts have run ahead of the results
proj:under:-16034:4429160.text: Your starters have landed under their projections on the season. The Texans defense has quietly beaten its number while De'Von Achane has missed his by the widest margin on the roster, which is the gap doing most of the damage. Weight the defense, discount Achane. One of those two is being graded on a different curve.

lineup:B:3916148:w7.title: Mostly sound, one Week 7 exception
lineup:B:3916148:w7.text: Your lineup calls have been among the better ones here, so this is a narrow complaint. Week 7 is it: Derrick Henry started at running back and had a quiet afternoon while Tony Pollard went off on your bench. Pollard has since taken a starting slot and kept it, which is the rare regret that pays you back.

pos:WR2:RB8.title: Second-best receivers, last-place backs
pos:WR2:RB8.text: Your receivers rank second in the league and your running backs rank last, which is the whole story of this roster. The trade idea on this page aims squarely at it, and so does starting Derrick Henry this week into what FantasyPros grades the best running back matchup on the board. Six running backs, and not enough of them.

proj:under:4239993:4870808.title: Slightly under forecast, and fixable
proj:under:4239993:4870808.text: Your starters have come in a little short of projection this season, and both ends of it are sitting on your bench. Tee Higgins has been beating his number while Jeremiyah Love has been missing his, and Higgins is the one ESPN wants in your flex this week. The fix is a seat change, not a trade.

lineup:C:4248528:w1.title: The points you left in Week 1
lineup:C:4248528:w1.text: Worth tightening, though the worst of it is ancient history: Week 1, Quinshon Judkins in the flex for a quiet afternoon while Christian Watson posted a big number on your bench. The recap formally retracted its opinion of that Judkins flex once it started paying off, so consider the matter closed.

pos:TE1:RB7.title: Best tight end in the league, thin at back
pos:TE1:RB7.text: Trey McBride has given you the top tight end production in this league while running back ranks seventh, so that is where the help should go. You carry six running backs, which means the problem is quality and not quantity. You have the bodies; what you need is one of them to be good.

proj:under:4248528:4569173.title: The forecasts have been too kind
proj:under:4248528:4569173.text: Your lineup has fallen well short of its projections this season. Christian Watson has been beating his number while Rhamondre Stevenson has been well short of his, and Stevenson is on New England's bye this week anyway. Trust the Watson projection and treat Stevenson's as aspirational.

lineup:C:2577417:w10.title: You won the week you got wrong
lineup:C:2577417:w10.text: This is the clearest fix on your page: more points have sat on your bench this season than on anyone else's. Week 10 is the headline, when Bryce Young started at quarterback and Dak Prescott put up a huge day behind him. You won that week anyway, which is the funniest possible outcome.

pos:K2:QB8.title: Your kicker outranks your quarterback room
pos:K2:QB8.text: Kicker ranks second in the league and quarterback ranks last, which is not the order those two are supposed to go in. The fix is free: Dak Prescott is on your bench and FantasyPros has him third among quarterbacks this week. Start him.

proj:under:4361050:4047650.title: The biggest projection gap in the league
proj:under:4361050:4047650.text: Your starters have missed their forecasts by more than anyone else's this season, and it is not subtle. Isaiah Likely has been beating his number while DK Metcalf has been well short of his. The tight end spot is in good hands either way; the receiver slot is where the projections keep getting it wrong, and Metcalf on the bench this week is the projection and the lineup finally agreeing.
